mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for four consecutive weeks (-56.6 to -50.3). This momentum reflects an ongoing, gradual normalization of shopping and leisure activity that should persist mechanically into the next four weeks absent a new shock, pushing mean RETAIL_REC higher.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved monotonically each of the last four weeks
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the last 28 days despite the prior four-week monotonic improvement trend continuing unbroken.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility jumped sharply from -35.9 to -25.0 in the latest week, a 10.9-point gain far exceeding prior weekly steps. This signals a behavioral shift toward outdoor and discretionary activity that typically precedes similar gains in nearby retail and recreation footfall within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 10.9 points in the latest week versus prior weekly gains under 3 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 2 weeks following a PARKS week-on-week jump exceeding 10 points, or PARKS reverses and declines by more than 5 points in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES (-45.4 to -41.3) and TRANSIT (-76.9 to -72.3) indicates restored commuting patterns. The joint effect of more people traveling to work via transit compounds to generate greater incidental retail footfall near transit hubs and workplaces, more than either series alone would predict, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved in each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is not larger when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve jointly compared to periods when only one series improves, as measured by comparable historical weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September marks the end-of-summer return to routine in Madrid, with schools and offices resuming. The steady decline in RESIDENTIAL (23.4 to 20.0) reflects people spending less time at home as routines normalize, which seasonally correlates with increased retail and recreation trips over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined each of the last four weeks from 23.4 to 20.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 2 weeks even as RESIDENTIAL continues its decline, or RESIDENTIAL reverses upward while RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has been steadily improving (-24.1 to -18.3) without any sudden reversal, indicating no new containment restrictions have been imposed on essential mobility. Absent policy tightening, retail and recreation venues remain open and accessible, supporting continued near-term growth in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-on-week change does not fall below -5 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved every week over the snapshot with no reversal
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next week even though GROCERY_PHARM continues improving without a sudden drop, falsifying the no-restriction-implies-growth link.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined every week (23.4 to 20.0), serving as an inverse behavioral proxy for time spent outside the home. This ongoing reduction in home-bound time mechanically frees up time for retail and recreation activity, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell monotonically across all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its monotonic decline through the same period.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has improved slowly but remains deeply depressed (-72.3 at t-0w). If TRANSIT crosses above -70 points, it signals a meaningful threshold of restored public transport usage sufficient to materially boost downstream retail and recreation visits within two weeks, since transit is a key enabler of shopping trips in Madrid's dense urban core.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT reached -72.3 at t-0w after rising from -76.9 at t-3w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show accelerated growth in the two weeks following TRANSIT crossing above -70 points, or shows growth similar to pre-threshold weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If local authorities respond to rising September COVID case counts (implied by the plateauing pace of PARKS and WORKPLACES recovery) with renewed capacity restrictions on retail and leisure venues, the combination of a stalling WORKPLACES trend and any abrupt PARKS reversal would jointly signal a tightening regime that suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change falls below +1 point while PARKS simultaneously reverses downward by more than 5 points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES weekly gains have been shrinking (2.0, 0.8 points in last two weeks)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 4 weeks even when WORKPLACES stalls and PARKS reverses downward, indicating no policy-tightening suppression effect.
